title: After a Layoff: Severance, Notice Pay and Leave
description: Separate severance, notice pay, and leave after an India layoff; confirm each amount, the written basis, unresolved questions, and where to get advice.
lead: Last verified against the listed official sources on 28 October 2026. The guide does not provide a universal severance formula or promise a particular payment.
editorialFrame: A final settlement can place severance, notice pay, earned salary, leave treatment, reimbursements, and deductions next to one another. This guide itemizes those payment questions; for broader record-keeping and post-layoff follow-up, see the employment-documents guide. That does not make the items the same entitlement or guarantee that each is payable in every case. Start with the written termination notice, contract, payroll records, and the employer's itemised statement. Separate what is confirmed from what depends on a clause, a rule, or a disputed fact.

sections.heading: Name each payment instead of accepting one total
sections.content:
Ask the employer to itemise salary through the last day, any notice pay, severance or retrenchment compensation, leave encashment, approved reimbursements, bonus or incentive, deductions, and any other amount. For each line, request the period covered, gross amount, deduction, payment date, and contractual or statutory basis. One combined number can hide a missing period or an amount that is conditional.

Keep the employer's statement beside your payslips, contract, leave balance, bonus plan, and exit notice. Mark each line as paid, pending, disputed, or not applicable. Ask for a corrected statement if a date or amount does not match the record. Do not add a potential payment to your cash plan until the employer confirms it and the condition has been met.

sections.heading: Check notice pay against the written exit terms
sections.content:
Read the termination clause and any notice provision in the signed agreement. Ask whether the employer is requiring work during notice, releasing you early, or paying in lieu, and which dates the decision covers. Confirm whether notice is measured in calendar days, working days, or another defined period. Do not assume a resignation buyout clause applies in the same way to an employer-initiated exit.

If the employer cites a policy or legal provision, ask for its title and the section relied on. The Ministry's official labour-code guidance contains provisions and FAQs about employment matters, but the result for an individual can depend on coverage, worker classification, establishment, state rules, and the dates involved. Get a qualified adviser to review a disputed interpretation.

sections.heading: Ask what “severance” means in this statement
sections.content:
The word severance is often used informally for different payments. Ask whether the amount is a contractual benefit, a policy payment, a settlement, or a statutory payment. Request the clause, policy, or provision and any conditions, such as signing a release, completing a handover, or meeting a service threshold. Read those conditions before accepting that a stated amount is unconditional.

A statement that a payment is “full and final” deserves careful review. Ask whether it records receipt, resolves disputed claims, or asks you to waive rights. Do not sign a broad release without understanding it. The applicable rules may not be the same for every role or employer, so use the actual documents and qualified advice rather than a generic severance calculator.

sections.heading: Reconcile leave separately from notice
sections.content:
Request the recorded leave balance, the employer's treatment of each category, and the rule or policy used for encashment. Ask whether leave was used, carried forward, forfeited, or paid, and which dates are included. The Ministry FAQ says leave encashment is not part of allowances for the Code on Wages definition. That statement concerns wage classification; it does not alone decide how much leave is payable to a particular employee.

Compare the answer with leave statements and the applicable policy. If a balance changed near termination, ask for the dated transaction or explanation. Keep notice days and leave days separate unless the employer confirms their interaction. State-law and establishment-specific provisions may matter; where the records conflict, ask a qualified adviser to review the coverage and current rules.

sections.heading: Check tax and payroll deductions by category
sections.content:
Ask payroll which tax year and payment category it used for each amount, and request the tax deduction details. Compensation on termination may receive different treatment depending on what the payment represents and the person's facts. The Income Tax Department's salaried-individual guide for AY 2026–27 includes a section on compensation for termination, but it is an overview and not a complete answer for every payment or filing situation.

Keep the payslip, tax deduction certificate, final statement, and payment confirmation together. Compare the amounts credited to the bank with gross amounts and deductions, but do not infer that a tax deduction proves the legal entitlement was calculated correctly. Ask a qualified tax professional about exemptions, reporting, or a payment spanning tax years.

sections.heading: Put questions and deadlines in writing
sections.content:
Send one list of questions to the named HR or payroll contact. Identify the exact line, document, and date for each issue. Ask when a corrected statement or payment is expected and who will reply. If you disagree with a line, state what record you rely on and the specific correction requested. Keep a copy of all replies and avoid sending more personal data than needed to reconcile the claim.

If there is a short deadline, a release document, or a significant disputed amount, obtain individual legal advice promptly. A checklist cannot decide whether a payment is owed or how a tribunal might interpret a clause. Do not let an urgent request turn an unverified statement into an accepted fact. Keep confirmed amounts separate from unresolved items while you seek a reliable answer.

sections.heading: Last verified and source boundary
sections.content:
Last verified against the listed official sources on 28 October 2026. Labour-code FAQs explain some wage and leave classifications, while the Income Tax Department provides current salaried-return guidance for AY 2026–27. Neither source independently settles every contract, severance, or final-pay claim.

The source links below are primary government references. Check the latest official notification and the documents that apply to your employer, state, role, and termination date. If two sources appear to conflict, record the dates and ask a qualified adviser which rule governs your specific facts.

nextSteps: Ask for a line-by-line statement separating salary, notice pay, severance, leave, reimbursements, variable pay, deductions, and payment dates.
Compare each line with your contract, termination notice, payslips, leave record, and bonus terms; request the basis for amounts that do not reconcile.
Review any release or “full and final” wording and get qualified legal or tax advice for disputed rights, exemptions, deadlines, or significant amounts.

faqs.question: Is severance always owed after a layoff?
faqs.answer: Do not assume a universal payment. The answer can depend on written terms, current law, coverage, role, dates, and the facts.

faqs.question: Is notice pay the same as severance?
faqs.answer: They may be separate categories. Ask the employer to name each payment and identify the document or rule behind it.

faqs.question: Does leave encashment count as salary?
faqs.answer: Tax and labour-law classification are specific questions. The Ministry wage FAQ does not by itself determine your payable balance.

faqs.question: Can I sign a full-and-final statement?
faqs.answer: Read its effect first. Ask whether it only acknowledges receipt or also releases disputed claims, and get advice if unclear.
